title: KV arena compaction + async spillover paging to reduce fragmentation and tail cost
author: Amit Desai
description:
Motivation: production workloads show increasing KV cache memory fragmentation over long-running Dedicated/Private instances. Fragmentation and small-object churn lead to suboptimal resident set sizes and increased tail OOM/reclamation events. This PR implements a multi-pronged approach: (1) per-shard arena compaction pass to reduce fragmentation, (2) asynchronous spillover paging for cold KV shards to disk (or remote object store) with non-blocking evacuation, and (3) eviction priority integration with the scheduler so hot-vs-cold decisions factor in request-criticality and active KV references.

Design summary: arena compaction runs periodically and opportunistically when fragmentation ratio (wasted_bytes / total_allocated) > compaction_threshold. Compaction uses a lightweight bump-copy into a temporary contiguous arena per shard and swaps pointers under a shard-level writer lock (short-duration). For very large shards we apply a streaming compaction to avoid duplicate memory spikes. Async spillover writes LRU-eligible pages to a local spill file (configurable, default tmpfs-backed snapshot + background upload to S3-compatible store when configured). Spill operations are scheduled on the new async-pager thread pool and do not block request paths; read-miss promotion pulls pages back and rewrites to the arena. Eviction policy: added a two-tier score = alpha * recency_score + beta * fragmentation_penalty + gamma * request_priority. Scheduler hooks allow routes to mark requests as high-priority (e.g., interactive chat) so eviction favors lower-priority background workloads first.

Changes included: compact/ allocator and compaction engine, async pager and spill file manager, eviction policy refactor, scheduler integration (eviction hints + priority), new metrics (fragmentation_ratio, compaction_runs, spill_pages_written, spill_paging_latency), a benchmark harness for measuring fragmentation over time, e2e tests for correctness and data integrity, and documentation under docs/ops/kv-tuning.md.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for allocator invariants and compaction correctness - [x] Benchmarks: long-run fragmentation sim, spike allocation tests - [x] e2e test that simulates sustained small-key churn and verifies no OOM/regression - [x] Metrics + Prometheus integration - [x] Canary rollout plan documented

Rollout & safety: feature gated behind runtime flag kv_compaction_enabled and kv_async_spill_enabled. Default rollouts: disabled in Hosted by default, enabled in Dedicated as opt-in for customers that request memory optimization. Canary strategy: gradual enablement on 1 Dedicated pool -> 10% of traffic -> 50% -> full, with automatic rollback on sustained increase in tail latency or >2% increase in 95th-token latency, or any crash.

Notes on scope: this PR focuses on allocator mechanics and the pager; follow-ups will add pluggable remote object stores for spill, tunable compaction strategies per workload, and telemetry-driven auto-tuning.

References: ENG-4123 (fragmentation dashboard), ENG-4199 (scheduler eviction hooks), SUP-7782 (customer incident describing repeated reclamation events).

review_comments: Sofia Park: Can we bound compaction CPU to avoid contention with inference? Suggested a token-bucket limiter for compaction worker quota.

Amit Desai: Added a CPU budget controller and made compaction background threads respect runtime 'compaction_cpu_pct' (default 5%). See compaction_engine.cpp - added unit test to ensure budget enforcement.
Liam O'Connor: Async pager looks good, but what's the failure mode if spill file IO is slow? Need backpressure so we don't just queue unbounded pages.

Amit Desai: Pager now exposes max_queue_bytes and backpressure signals to the scheduler so eviction will slow down and trigger migration to a different pool when exceeded. Also added metrics for pager_queue_length.
Elena Ruiz: We should make the eviction scoring weights configurable per-deployment. Also requested more comments on invariants in allocator.h.
Amit Desai: Added runtime flags for alpha/beta/gamma and expanded comments in allocator.h describing invariants and atomicity guarantees.
release_notes:
- Added per-shard arena compaction to reduce KV cache fragmentation.
- Added asynchronous spillover paging to move cold pages off-heap to spill files with background upload support.
- Eviction policy extended to account for fragmentation and request priority.
- New metrics: fragmentation_ratio, compaction_runs, spill_pages_written, pager_queue_length.
perf_benchmarks: Fragmentation test (48h churn): resident set reduced from 18.2GB -> 12.7GB (30% lower) with compaction+spill enabled
Tail OOM events: observed 6->0 incidents in 7-day synthetic replay (internal cluster)
Throughput: negligible change (<0.5%) on p99 throughput under steady-state workloads
rollout_plan: Gated rollout: 1) merge behind runtime flags; 2) enable on single Dedicated pool for 24h; 3) monitor frag metrics, tail OOMs, p95 latency; 4) 10% traffic for 48h; 5) 50% traffic 48h; 6) full; automatic rollback triggers described in description.
risk_mitigation: Feature flags to disable compaction and async spill at runtime
Pager queue backpressure wired to scheduler so eviction slows instead of OOMing
Canary with strict SLA/telemetry thresholds and automatic rollback
Extensive unit + e2e tests plus a long-run bench harness included
